# Class A — the ledger

Every class-A reading from `variae-lectiones-transcript.md` (apparatus pages [i]–vi, printed pp. 6–242), resolved against our own transcripts.

## ⚠ The rule this ledger exists to enforce

**NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN APPLIED, AND NOTHING HERE MAY BE APPLIED SILENTLY.**

Our transcripts record **the 1853 plate**. Class A records **the manuscript behind it**. They are two witnesses and the edition needs both. The 1853 says class A is *pro veris habenda* — "to be held as the true ones" — and it may well be right, but "the editor of our base text thinks his own text is wrong here" is an argument to be made in an apparatus, not a licence to overwrite a transcript. **Any change to a transcript is a separate, argued commit, and it is Wilson's decision, not a session's.**

Status values: `applied` is never used and should stay never used. Everything is `recorded` (located in our files, difference confirmed), `recorded — not locatable` (the apparatus's line number does not resolve), or `structural` (not a word-change but a layout or content claim).

---

## 1. Readings that change the WORDS — the ones that would alter our text

| printed | our transcript reads | apograph reads | our file | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6. 15 | `Μνήσθητι` present | *dele* | front | a whole word dropped |
| 6. 20 | `τοῦ ἁγίου φροντιστηρίου τούτου` | `τῆς ἁγίας μονῆς ταύτης` | front | **Latin sides with the plate** (*Collegii*) |
| 6. 22 | `δοξάζοντι` | `δοξάσαντι` | front | present → aorist |
| 12. 16 | `φροντιστήριον` | `συνέδριον` | front | the same substitution as 6. 20, different word |
| 12. 26 | `τῶν νῦν` + `Βασιλικόν` | `τῶν τανῦν`, *dele* `Βασιλικόν` | front | **Latin sides with the plate** (*Regium*) |
| 12. 27, 28 | `ἐλεημοσύνης Βασιλικῆς` | *dele* | front | second deletion of a royal reference |
| 12. 29 | `Φροντιστήρια` | `Συνέδρια` | front | third of the φροντιστήριον set |

| 242. 6 | words the 1853 bracketed **as its own conjecture** | *dele uncinas*; `τῆς` before `διανοίας` | evening | ⚠ see §3 |

---

## 2. ⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE: THE 1853 DROPPED HEBREW THAT STOOD IN ANDREWES' TEXT

**This overturns a standing correction in our own map, and the correction has now been reversed in `STRUCTURE.md`.**

`STRUCTURE.md` carried, and the project memory repeated, the line: *"CORRECTION: NO Hebrew in the main text at 198/200/212 (confirmed by eye) — the Hebrew is Variae Lectiones §A apparatus only."*

**Half right, and the wrong half is the important half.** It is true that no Hebrew is printed at those places in the 1853 — our eyes were not deceived. But class A is *"variæ lectiones quæ in textu ipso occurrunt"* — **readings that occur in the text itself**, held to be the true ones. So what the note actually records is that **the Hebrew stands in the manuscript's text and the 1853 edition left it out.**

The Hebrew class A restores, in full:

| printed | what the MS has | gloss |
|---|---|---|
| 38. 3 | `אדאג` in the margin opposite | Heb. for `μεριμνῶ` — "I am anxious" |
| 76. 4 | *adde* `יצר טוב` after `Φαντασίαν καλὴν` | **the rabbinic *yetzer ha-tov***, the good inclination |
| 86 (ult., penult.), 88 | *Voces Hebrææ Græcis respondentes in altero στοίχῳ subjiciuntur* | a Hebrew column set under the Greek |
| 92. 10, 13, 16 | `תהום` · `תוהו` · `בוהו` before `αἱ ἄβυσσοι` · `γῆ` · `τὰ χλοερὰ` | **Genesis i. 2** — the deep, and *tohu wa-bohu* |
| 96. 25–31 | a full Greek–Hebrew bilingual column (below) | the vocabulary of sin |
| 152. 8 | `ואתה תעל משחת חיי` **in place of the Greek** | **Jonah ii. 7**, under the MS's own heading `Τοῦ Ἰωνᾶ` |
| 192. 17, 18 | *Hebraice leguntur*; the Greek is at the foot of the page | the plate has inverted the MS's priority |
| 198 (before line 1) | `אל תשחית` / `הצילני` ‖ `תעל משחת` / `חיי` | glossed by the 1853 itself: *ne perdas / libera me* ‖ *subleva de corruptione / vitam meam* |
| 200 (after line 8) | `אל תשחית` / `הצילני` | |
| 202. 15 | `הצילני` **in place of** `ῥῦσαί με` | |
| 210 (before last line) | *eadem Hebraice* — Ps. lxxxvi. 11 | |
| 212. 1 | `יראתי כסלתי` after `ὁ φόβος μου` | |

**The bilingual column at printed 96. 25–31** — seven Greek names for sin, each with its Hebrew:

`φαντασίαν` יצר · `σφάλμα` שגגה · `ἐνοχὴν πταῖσμα` אשם · `ἁμαρτίαν` חטאה · `παράβασιν` פשע · `ἀδικίαν` עון · `βδέλυγμα` תועבה

That is the standard Hebrew vocabulary of sin — *yetzer, shegagah, asham, chata'ah, pesha, avon, to'evah* — set out as a lexicon. **It is not in the printed book at all.**

⚠ **Consequences, all of them for Wilson, none of them for a session:**
1. The edition's claim to carry four scripts is **understated, not overstated**. Andrewes' Hebrew was systematic where the 1853 shows it as occasional.
2. The `יצר` at 96. 25 and the `יצר טוב` at 76. 4 mean Andrewes was **reading his own *φαντασία* through the rabbinic doctrine of the two inclinations.** That is a substantive theological finding about the *Preces*, not a textual footnote.
3. **Whether to restore any of it is a decision about what edition this is** — a faithful reprint of the 1853, or a critical text of Andrewes. The project has never had to answer that question before, because until now the two coincided.
4. ✅ **All Hebrew here was RE-READ at native resolution on the Toronto scan, 2026-08-10, and every form is confirmed — nothing changed.** The look-alike sorts (ד/ר, ב/כ, ה/ח) are cleanly separable there. `אדאג` at 38. 3, which had been secure on sense but not on its sorts, is now secure on both. ⚠ Still unread because nothing sets them: the `אל תשחית` / `הצילני` cluster at 198–202 and `יראתי כסלתי` at 212. 1. See `SOURCE-IMAGES.md`.

---

## 3. ⚠ The 1853 prints its own conjectures, and the manuscript overrules them

Three places where class A is not correcting a misreading but **withdrawing an editorial invention**:

- **100. 10** — the plate has `[στρατιώτας]`, marked *ex conjectura nostra*; the MS reads `βιαστάς`. Soldiers for violent men.
- **104. 6** — the plate has `[οὐκ εἰς τέλος]`, *ex conjectura nostra*; the MS reads `οὐκ ἀεί`.
- **242. 6** — *dele uncinas quibus has voces e conjectura nostra additas notavimus*, and read `τῆς` before `διανοίας`.
- **202. 3 &c., 9, 13** — ⚠ the strongest of the set: *`Notæ numerales non leguntur; ex Vers. Angl. a nobis desumpta sunt.`* **The numerals in our transcript of printed 202 are not in the manuscript at all** — the 1853 editor took them from an English version. Anything our files infer from that numbering is inference from an editor's scaffolding.
- **204. 17–23** — and the MS's own numbers, where it has them, run **`2, 1, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7`**, not in sequence.

**To the project's credit, the discipline already in force handles all of this correctly**: the transcripts record brackets as printed and never silently mend. But `[στρατιώτας]` and `[οὐκ εἰς τέλος]` were transcribed as the 1853's supplied readings, and are now known to be **wrong** supplied readings. That is worth a line in the introduction.

---

## 4. ⚠ Class A and class C collide — and the collision is NOT resolved here

At eight lines a class-A reading and a Drake marginal address the same words:

| printed | class A (the MS's text) | class C (Drake, *in ora libri*) |
|---|---|---|
| 34. 27 | `τὰ ἔργα` → `τὸ πλάσμα` | `τὰ ἔργα] τὸ πλάσμα (τὰ ἔργα superscriptum est)` |
| 34. 28 | `ὁμοίωμα` + point | `ὁμοίωμα] ὁμοίωσιν` |
| 50. 18 | `προσδοκίας` → `ἐλπίδος` | `προσδοκίας.` |
| 52. ult. | *dele* `ἃ μέλλει ἀποθανεῖν` | `μέλλει ἀποθανεῖν.` |
| 104. 3 | *dele* `οὐχ ἑκὼν` | `οὐχ ἑκὼν.` |
| 162. 16 | `ὑπερέχουσα` → `ὑπερβάλλουσα` | `ὑπερέχουσα in marg. legitur` |
| 170. 16 | `ἀνομίας` → `ἁμαρτίας` | `ἁμαρτίας] ἀνομίας` |
| 190. 13 | `ἀνόμων` → `ἀνομιῶν` | `ἀνόμων] in marg. tantum` |
| 224. 8 | `ἑσπερινὴ` → `δειλινή` | `δειλινή] ἑσπερινή` |

**The tempting theory** — that the printed 1853 text has in places adopted **Drake's marginal reading** rather than the manuscript's, so that our transcript at those lines is a later hand, not Andrewes — is **attractive, partly supported, and not established.** It cannot be settled from the printed apparatus alone, because **the direction of class C's `]` is ambiguous**: Drake wrote in the margin *of the apograph*, so his lemma should be the manuscript's reading, yet at 34. 27 and 224. 8 the lemma is what the *printed* text has, which points the other way.

⚠ **Do not build an argument on these collisions until the manuscript itself has been seen.** They are recorded here as a question, in the same spirit in which the volume's cruces are left as cruces. **The brief's standing instruction — "class C is evidence about Drake, not about Andrewes; never apply it to the text" — is unaffected and still governs.**

Worth noting for whoever does see the MS: **Drake was not a mere normaliser.** He collates against the **Wechel** edition (pp. 4. 20; 170. 28), cites **Aquila, Theodotion and Symmachus** at p. 134. 23–24, and traces the Prayer of Manasses to the *Apostolic Constitutions* II. 22 *apud Zonaram* (Paris, 1618). The brief's "later hand with a normalising agenda" is accurate about his aim and understates his competence.

---

## 5. Structural claims — no words change, but the page does

- **10. 3 – 14. 11** — *indicem quendam precum constituere videntur*: this stretch is **an index of prayers**, marked with the MS's dot-symbols, pointing to pp. 186, 190, 198, 208, 214, 220, and *fortasse* 234 or 236. **Our transcripts render it as text.** If it is an index it is apparatus, and Prototype B would set it differently.
- **32. 27** — after `ἐποίησα` **a ruled line**, *quasi spatium ad enumeranda peccata reservatum esset* — a blank left for the reader to enumerate his own sins. **A deliberate silence in the book, and our transcript does not show it.**
- **30. 19, 22** — `α΄`, `β΄` in the margin: the MS numbers parts with **Greek letters**, per the preface's principle iii. Our files use arabic throughout.
- **62. 21–22 · 70. 12 · 74. 6–20 / 76. 5 · 82. 27 · 116. 1–4 · 156. 12 · 158. 4 · 174. 5–6 · 182. 11–15 · 186. 11–12 · 204. 1–2** — column and line re-arrangements; several say two facing sets are meant to answer one another *invicem*, which bears directly on the mirror's page-fit.
- **82. 27 – 84. 7 · 186. 14–16, 21 sqq. · 188. 1–3 · 190. 26** — ⚠ ***manu posteriori addita sunt***: the intercessions naming `τῶν Παναγίων Βερκίγγ` and `Οὐϊντονίας` (**Winchester** — Andrewes' own see) are **a later hand in the manuscript.** Whether they are Andrewes adding to his own book or someone else adding to it is exactly the sort of question the introduction should raise and not answer.
- **70. 19 · 72. 5, 13, 17 · 94 · 96. 9, 11 · 106–110 · 130–134 · 150–152 · 164. ult. · 170. 2 · 218. 6, 12, 13** — words to be set *litteris grandioribus* / *majusculis*: the MS's own display hierarchy (`Τοῦ Μωϋσέως`, `Τοῦ Ἰώβ`, `Τῆς Χαναναίας`, `Τοῦ Μυριοταλάντου`, `Τοῦ Τελωνοῦ`, `Τοῦ Ἀσώτου`, the prophets, `Τοῦ Δαβὶδ`, `Τοῦ Σαλομῶν`, `Τοῦ Μανασσῆ`). **These are speakers' names — the Publican, the Prodigal, the Canaanite woman, the Debtor of Ten Thousand Talents — and the manuscript displays them.** The 1853 flattens them into the text. For a mirror edition this is a live typographic decision.
- **128. 10 · 136. 4, 18** — cross-references to an **English version in Andrewes' *Works*, vol. vii, pp. 290, 293**. A witness the project has not consulted.

---

## 6. Not locatable

None. Every class-A citation resolves to a page held in `part1/`, which covers printed 1–263 continuously. Line numbers were **not** individually verified against our line counts — the apparatus counts lines of the 1853's Greek column, and our transcripts preserve those lines, but a line-by-line audit is a separate job and is **not** claimed here.

body:
# Class B — the spacing record against our unit boundaries

Class B is *"Intervalla sive spatia, **quæ mentem auctoris sæpius indicant**"* — the intervals and spaces, **which often show the author's mind**. It is the manuscript's own record of where Andrewes left air on the page, and it is the highest-value class in the apparatus for the edition's *structure*, as CONVENTIONS §13 anticipated.

**Scope: printed pp. 2–250 only** — the whole extent of the apograph.

## ⚠ First, the negative result the brief asked for

The brief asked that class B be weighed against **the boundaries we chose ourselves** — naming **§28's** and **Part III's §2/§3 cut**.

**Class B cannot speak to either.** §28 is at printed 361–367 and the Part III §2/§3 cut is at printed 416, both far outside the apograph's *usque ad pag. 250*. **Those two boundaries remain exactly as well or badly supported as they were, and this pass adds nothing to them.** They stand on our own reasoning — which, in §3's case, was independently confirmed from the plate (the half-blank page at 424) and does not need the manuscript.

Everything below therefore concerns **Part I only**.

---

## 1. Where the manuscript's silences fall, against our files

Our Part I files divide: **front** 1–29 · **day1** 30–69 · **day2** 70–91 · **day3** 92–105 · **day4** 106–129 · **day5** 130–147 · **day6** 148–167 · **day7** 168–195 · **deprecation** 196–219 · **evening** 220–251 · **meditations** 252–263.

The manuscript's **blank pages and blank leaves** — its major articulations, as distinct from ordinary line-spaces:

| printed | the MS does | our boundary | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| after **184** | ⚠ ***tria sunt folia non scripta*** — **three blank leaves, six blank pages, the largest silence in the manuscript** | mid-**day7** | ⚠⚠ **MISMATCH — see §2** |
| **190**, after line 4 | *duæ paginæ non scriptæ* | mid-**day7** | ⚠ **MISMATCH — see §2** |
| **196** | *pagina non scripta sequitur* | **deprecation** opens at 196 | near-match, offset by a page |
| **207** | *pagina non scripta sequitur* | mid-**deprecation** | ⚠ and see §3 — this is the only odd page in the whole class |
| **212** | *pagina non scripta sequitur* | mid-**deprecation** | unmarked by us |
| after **218** | *duæ paginæ non scriptæ* | **deprecation** ends 219, **evening** opens 220 | ✅ **MATCH** |
| after **236** | *duæ paginæ non scriptæ* | mid-**evening** | unmarked by us |
| after **248** | *pagina non scripta* | mid-**evening** | unmarked by us |
| **250**, after line 16 | *nova pagina incipit cum verbis* `Γνῶσιν καὶ πίστιν` | mid-**evening** | the apograph ends here |

**One clean match, two clear mismatches, five divisions we do not mark at all.**

## 2. ⚠⚠ The three blank leaves after printed 184

This is the finding of the class-B pass.

**What our transcript has at the foot of printed 184:**

> καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι, / οὔτε κραυγὴ, / οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι, / **ὅτι τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθον.**

Revelation xxi. 4 — *and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* **A terminal text if the book has one.** And the manuscript answers it with **six blank pages**, more air than it gives anything else.

**What follows, at printed 186:** `ΑΓΑΘΥΝΟΝ, ΚΥΡΙΕ` — the great personal intercession, Barking and Pembroke Hall and Southwell and Westminster, Andrewes' own churches under Greek names.

⚠ **Our own transcript already noticed that this is a different kind of thing.** The note at the head of printed 186 in `day7-transcript.md` reads *"the great personal intercession (cf. Day 3 pp. 98–101)"* — it cross-references it out of Day 7 to a different day, because it does not belong where it sits. **The manuscript agrees, and says so with three blank leaves; our file runs straight through it.**

Likewise the two blank pages after **190. 4**, which fall immediately after the close of a list (`προαιρέσεις, / ἐπιχειρήσεις, / ἔξοδον, καὶ εἴσοδον, / κάθεδραν, καὶ ἔγερσιν.`) — a clean end, and the MS marks it.

**What this does NOT mean.** It does not mean `day7-transcript.md` is wrong. The file records the 1853 plate faithfully and the plate does run continuously. **The manuscript and the printed book disagree about where Day 7 ends, and that disagreement is a fact about the edition, not an error in our files.** Whether to re-cut the file, or to record the division in the apparatus and leave the file alone, is **Wilson's call** — and it is the same question the Hebrew raises in `CLASS-A-ledger.md` §2: is this edition a faithful reprint of the 1853, or a critical text of Andrewes?

**A pragmatic note for whoever decides:** re-cutting a transcript re-cuts its English, and Part I's English is line-keyed page by page. The cost is real. The cheaper and probably better move is to **record the MS's divisions in the apparatus and in the print design** — Prototype B has spreads to spend, and six blank manuscript pages are exactly the sort of thing a mirror edition can honour typographically without touching a transcript.

## 3. ⚠ `p. 207` — the only odd page in class B

Every other citation in classes A and B is an **even** printed page, because Part I sets Greek on the verso (even) and Latin on the recto (odd), and the apograph is Greek only. **`p. 207. pagina non scripta sequitur` is the sole exception in the entire apparatus.**

Three possibilities, and this file does not choose between them:
1. a misprint for **206** or **208** — the likeliest, and the volume has proved itself capable of exactly this class of slip repeatedly;
2. the editor briefly citing by his own **Latin** page because that is where the leaf-break falls;
3. something about the manuscript's own foliation at that point.

**Left as a crux.** It costs nothing and resolves nothing to guess.

## 4. What class B corroborates rather than challenges

**The seven days.** Class B does **not** mark the day-divisions with spacing — and it should not, because the preface's principle **iv** says *`Dies sua quisque nota astronomica distinguitur`*: **each day is distinguished by its own astronomical sign**, a different device entirely. **Our day boundaries at printed 30 · 70 · 92 · 106 · 130 · 148 · 168 are corroborated by principle iv and are untouched by class B's silence about them.** This is worth stating plainly, because a naive reading of class B would take the absence of spacing at those pages as evidence against our cuts. It is not.

**The deprecation/evening cut at 218–220** is confirmed outright by two blank pages.

## 5. The ordinary spacing record — for the typesetter, not the editor

The bulk of class B (apparatus vii–ix) is a line-by-line register of ordinary spaces, larger spaces, and lines run together without space: e.g. *`p. 124. lin. 3, 4, 6, 7, 11, 12, 17, 18, 24, 25, sine intervallo`*; *`p. 172. post lin. 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, et post 14 et 25 majus`*; *`p. 36. post lin. 1, 5 majus, 18, 22, 25, 29`*. It distinguishes at least three weights — *spatium* · *majus spatium / majus intervallum* · *breve spatium* — and records where lines the plate separates are **joined** (*colligantur*, 192. 11–13 and 14–16) or where lines the plate joins are **separated**.

⚠ **This is the single most useful document in the apparatus for Prototype B**, and it is entirely unexploited. The mirror's whole difficulty is page-fit: every spread must fit or the verso/recto mirror silently flips. **Class B is a page-by-page account, from the author's own book, of where the vertical air is meant to go and how much of it** — which is precisely the variable a typesetter has to guess at otherwise.

**Recommendation, for a later print session and not for now:** when `transcript2tex.py` is finally generalised, feed class B in as a spacing table keyed to printed page and line. It will not solve page-fit, but it converts an arbitrary choice into a documented one, and where a spread will not fit, it says which spaces Andrewes cared about and which he did not.

---

## What is owed

- **Nothing has been changed.** No transcript re-cut, no boundary moved, no English touched.
- **Wilson's calls, both of them the same question in two coats:** whether the manuscript's divisions after printed 184 and 190 should re-cut `day7`, and whether the Hebrew of `CLASS-A-ledger.md` §2 should be restored. Both ask: **faithful reprint of the 1853, or critical text of Andrewes?** The project has never had to answer that, because until this pass the two coincided.
- **`p. 207`** goes on the pre-print list as a crux.

# Brightman 1903 as a collation witness — pilot, method, and the anchor table

**Pilot run 2026-08-04. Five probes, four hits, one crux solved. Nothing applied.**

Source: `archive.org/details/bwb_KP-665-232` — F. E. Brightman, *The Preces Privatae of Lancelot Andrewes*, Methuen, London, 1903, 472 pp. Full text public. Working copy of the OCR: `bwb_KP-665-232_hocr_searchtext.txt.gz` (the `_djvu.txt` endpoint 500s; the hOCR searchtext gz works).

---

## 1. What Brightman is, and is not, as a witness

**He is NOT a witness to the Greek or Latin text.** He prints none of it — *"no attempt has been made to mark the distinction between the Greek and the Latin of the original"* — confirmed mechanically: **zero Greek runs and zero Hebrew runs in 755 KB of OCR across all 472 pages.** He cannot correct a transcription.

**He IS a strong witness to four things we actually need:**

1. **Construal.** An independent English of the same book. Where his reading and ours diverge, one of us has misread.
2. **Scripture references.** Marginal refs throughout, with `heb.` / `sept.` / `vulg.` added where the original departs from the English Bible. ⚠ This bears directly on our worst problem — the volume's dense bad-reference stretches, and the three places where it proves its own misprints.
3. **Non-scriptural sources.** He identifies them, and his index names the **edition Andrewes used**. This is what the pre-print attribution questions need.
4. **The manuscripts.** He collates **O** (Oxford 1675) against **H** (Harleian), **L** (Laudian), **W/Wy**, and **S** (Stokes). Our Part III is the Harley recension, so **H-vs-O variants in his notes speak directly to Part III against Part II.**

---

## 2. The pilot — four findings

### ✅ 2.1 §35 Bradwardine — confirmed, and sourced exactly
Our §35 (printed 370) identified Bradwardine. Brightman's note: *"P. 192. Thomas Bradwardine was archbishop of Canterbury for five weeks in 1349. His work* de causa Dei contra Pelagium et de virtute causarum, *from which the present passage is taken…"* — with the marginal ref **`T. Bradwardine de virtute causarum ii cor. 39`** and, in his index, the edition: **Saville, London 1618**.
**Gain:** the work, the exact corollary, and the edition Andrewes had.

### ✅ 2.2 §39's Fulgentius attribution — CORROBORATED; our Augustine doubt answered
Our notes flagged the 1853's `ex Fulgentii l. i. ad Mon.` as **UNVERIFIED and "looks like Augustine"** (*De Doctrina Christiana* IV), and kept it as printed. Brightman, working independently from the sources, **also gives Fulgentius** — index: **`Fulgentius of Ruspe, S. (Migne Patr. lat. lxv.), 257`**, and a note at his p. 257. 9 identifying him as bishop of Ruspe, 508–533. His introduction paraphrases the passage as ours reads it — *"it is rather by the piety of his prayers for himself and his flock than by fluency of speech…"*
**Gain:** a pre-print item moves from *doubted* to *independently corroborated*. (PL 65 is Fulgentius's volume and contains *Ad Monimum*.) The transcript is unchanged either way; what changes is the note.

### ✅✅ 2.3 Part III §1's `mundam` — confirmed as a HARLEIAN-vs-OXFORD variant
Our Part III §1 finding recorded, among five substantive divergences from §23, that the faith-catalogue **adds `mundam` and drops `vincentem mundum`**. Brightman's note:

> **`P. 189. 6. H reads mundam 'pure'; O, vincentem mundum.`**

**This is an independent confirmation of one of our own five divergences — and it names the mechanism.** H = Harleian, O = Oxford 1675. ⚠ **It corroborates the structural claim that Part III is the Harley recension**, from a witness who had the Harleian manuscript itself.

### ✅✅ 2.4 THE `Isaac` CRUX AT PRINTED 425 IS SOLVED — the word is **Mosis**
Our §4 note (printed 425): *"`Cantemus Domino Isaac et Israelitarum` (Exod. xv. 2) — Isaac has no part in the song at the Red Sea and no construal makes him fit. Translated straight, difficulty left visible, on the pre-print list."*

Brightman's text, in the same Benedictus-catena and in the same position:

> *"Blessed be the Lord **(of Jethro)** Ex. xviii 10"*
> *"I will sing unto the Lord **(of Moses and the Israelites)** Ex. xv 1"*

**The catena tags each text with whose blessing it is, and the reading is `Mosis et Israelitarum`** — Exod. xv. 1, *"Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD."* ⚠ **`Isaac` is an error in the printed line**, and the reference is off by one as well (**xv. 1**, not xv. 2).

**Kept as printed in the transcript, per standing discipline.** What changes is that the English's note can now say what the reading must be instead of leaving the difficulty merely visible. **The crux comes off the pre-print list.**

### ⊘ 2.5 The garbled Hebrew at printed 386 — NOT testable from the OCR
Brightman **marks Hebrew by printing its translation in italic** (preface §4). ⚠ **Italics do not survive OCR into plain text.** So `חזתלת` → `תוחלת` cannot be checked from the text dump; it needs his **page images**. Recorded as a method limit, not a negative result.

**But the same probe paid anyway.** His p. 106 is our §41 (printed 386), and his margin supplies the source identifications our transcript lacked: **`Cic. de senect. 11`** (Cato's daily audit) · **`Auson. Idyll.`** · **`Ps. lxxvii 6`** · **`Cp. Lucian Hermotimus 64`** · **`S. Aug. Serm. XX 2`** · **`Ecclus. xxiii 2`** · **`1 Cor. xi 31`** · **`S. Greg. Nyss. de orat. dom. 1`**.
✅ **THE SENECA DIVERGENCE IS CLOSED (Wilson located it, 2026-08-04).** ***Seneca.*** is printed in the plate at **printed 385**, and the attribution is **correct**: sentence 1, `Deprehendas te oportet, antequam emendes`, is **Seneca, *Ep. Mor.* 28. 10**. **So the plate is right and Brightman's margin is simply short an authority** — his silence never indicated an error, and nothing here was ever ours to correct. ⚠ Seneca's own lead-in credits *«Initium est salutis notitia peccati»* to **EPICURUS**, which makes the §41 catena's chain **Epicurus → Seneca → Andrewes** — an introduction asset. ⚠⚠ **Sentence 2** (`Ignotum ulcus in deterius abit, et curatione destituitur`) is **not** in *Ep.* 28 and, on Wilson's search, **occurs ONLY IN ANDREWES** — so the one `*Seneca.*` tag covers two sentences of which **only the first is Seneca's**, the second amplifying his metaphor (the sore never found festers and goes uncured) and quite possibly being Andrewes' own. **Stated at the strength the evidence bears: unattested elsewhere, NOT "Andrewes' own"** — a florilegium or commonplace source is not excluded. **The tag is kept as printed** (§39 *Fulgentius* rule: an over-reaching attribution is flagged, never trimmed to fit); the note carries what the tag does not.

---

## 3. Method — why a linear pass is the wrong shape

**Brightman rearranged the book on principle** (preface §3), and **his notes and index are keyed to his own pagination**. So there is no mechanical crosswalk from his page to our printed page. The anchors below make the point:

| Brightman p. | our printed p. | section |
|---|---|---|
| 106 | 386 | Part II §41 (*Monita* / evening examination) |
| 189 | ~403 | **Part III §1** (*Confessio Fidei*) |
| 192 | 370 | Part II §35 (Bradwardine) |
| 257 | 380 | Part II §39 (*Ante Concionem*, Fulgentius) |

His 189 < 192 < 257 maps to our 403 > 370 < 380. **The order is genuinely scrambled; a page-by-page collation would mean building a 472-page crosswalk first.**

**The right shape is a QUESTION-DRIVEN pass.** Every hit above came from grepping a proper name or a distinctive phrase — cheap, and aimed at items that already matter. Run our existing lists through him:

1. the **pre-print verification list**
2. the running list of **wrong and doubtful references** (Part III §2 alone has 4 demonstrably wrong + 6 doubtful — the densest in the volume)
3. the **attributions** (§39 done; §35 done)
4. the **cruces** (425 done; `p. 207`; `Tuâ.` at 421; the unnumbered witness at 423)
5. the **five plate defects** in the watch list — ⚠ especially **printed 370/371, where a heading and an opening are MISSING from the 1853**. Brightman had the manuscripts; he may simply have the missing text.
6. **class A's H/L variants** — his notes are the second opinion on the Wright apograph's readings, from different manuscripts.

**Accumulate the anchor table as a by-product.** Each lookup fixes one (his page ↔ our printed page) pair at zero marginal cost. If enough structure emerges, a fuller pass becomes cheap later. If it never does, we lost nothing.

⚠ **Two standing limits:**
- **Anything depending on italics — i.e. ALL of the Hebrew — needs his page images, not the OCR.** This folds into the 600-dpi digitization job that already gates both books.
- Brightman is a **witness, not an authority**. He is emending from manuscripts we have not seen, and he says himself that where he adds words to complete a sense he brackets them. **The transcripts still record the 1853 plate; nothing here writes back to them.**

---

## 3a. ✅ THE FLAG-LIST PASS — run 2026-08-04 on Opus, Wilson's go.

> ⚠ **The old header here read "Nothing applied." That was true on the day and is no longer true** (corrected 2026-08-09). Every finding below has since been carried into the relevant section's English flags — §23, §26, §35, §41, Part III §1 and §4 all state their results in place. **What is still true, and is the rule: nothing was applied to a TRANSCRIPT.** The 1853 plate stands as printed everywhere; the repairs live in the English layer's notes.

### ⚠⚠ The method finding, which is worth more than any single repair
**THE VOLUME REPAIRS ITS OWN DEFECTS ACROSS THE RECENSION BOUNDARY.** Part III is the Harley recension of Part II's penitential matter (§1 : §23+§38 :: §2 : §17 :: §4 : §24). **So where Part II's plate is defective, Part III may carry the same passage intact** — a free, internal, entirely unused repair route. It resolved watch item #4 below before Brightman was even needed. **Check the recension parallel FIRST on any Part II defect; it costs nothing.**

### ⚠ And the hard limit on Brightman
**He prints no Greek and no Latin, so he can NEVER repair a lost Latin or Greek word** — only a reference, an attribution, a construal, or a sense. Watch items **1 (printed 239, cut-off Latin recto)** and **2 (printed 210, ink damage)** therefore **stay open for the digitization regardless**, and no amount of collation will close them.
⚠ **His headings are HIS OWN** — preface §3: *"For titles, etc., which are printed in thick type… I am responsible."* **Never import a Brightman heading as recovered text.**

### Watch items
| # | item | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | **printed 370/371** — "a heading AND an opening are missing" | ⚠ **DOWNGRADED.** Brightman's litany **also begins at "For the wounded in spirit"** — so **the opening is not lost; the litany does start there.** What is missing is a heading — and **his ("FOR THOSE IN AFFLICTION AND PERIL") is his own and cannot be used.** Restate the watch item as *heading only*. |
| 4 | **printed 339/340 §23** — missing antecedent + wanted *non tantum* | ✅✅ **RESOLVED, from TWO independent witnesses that agree verbatim.** Our own **Part III §1** reads `3. In Spiritum Sanctum, … Extrinsecus et invisibiliter, sed / Efficaciter et manifeste in / Nos operantem, / Illuminatione justitiæ, / Infusione gratiæ, / In Reprehensione, Doctrina, Tolerantia, Subventione…`; Brightman renders the same, *"in the Holy Ghost… from without and invisibly, but effectuously and manifestly operating upon us by illumination of righteousness, infusion of grace, in reproof, teaching, bearing with, help, witnessing with."* **The lost antecedent is the Holy Ghost** (our conjecture, confirmed) and **the lost hinge is `Extrinsecus et invisibiliter, sed`** — not a *non tantum*. ⚠ **`in Nos operantem` is accusative: our supplied `[in us]` should be `[upon us]`.** *Recommended correction, NOT applied.* |
| 5 | **printed 353 §26 V.7** — `omnia m` broken mid-word, book name lost | ✅✅ **CONFIRMED EXACTLY.** Brightman: *"Send not a cruel messenger unto us: **Prov. xvii 11** / but let all evils be put far away from our houses. **13**"* — **our reconstruction `omnia m[ala. Prov.] xvii. 11, 13` is right in every part.** |
| 1, 2 | printed 239, printed 210 | ⊘ **Not closable by Brightman** — see the hard limit above. Digitization only. |
| 0 | printed 386 garbled Hebrew | ⊘ Needs his **page images**; italics do not survive OCR. |

### References and attributions
- ✅ **§28 `[Dan. vi. 4.]` → `Dan. i. 8`.** Brightman: *"If not wholly from all; **Dan. i 8** — yet from dainties?"* Daniel refusing the king's meat. **Identified**; kept as printed.
- ✅ **§28 `tricesimam partem` — CONFIRMED as the reading**, with **Deut. xxvi. 12**, in a second witness who also declined to mend it. Our note said the choice between Andrewes' own reduction and a corruption of *tertiam* "cannot be settled from this witness." **It is now settled: it is the text.** The oddity is Andrewes'.
- ✅ **Part III §2 `Jo. ix. 30` → 31 CONFIRMED.** Brightman: *"But I am a sinner: **S. Jo. ix 31** and God heareth not sinners."*
- ✅ **Printed 425 `Isaac` → `Mosis`, Exod. xv. 1** (§2.4 above).
- ✅ **§39 Fulgentius corroborated**; ✅ **§35 Bradwardine sourced exactly** (§2.1–2.2 above).
- ⊘ No hit: Part III §2's `Marc. iv. 28` and `1 Cor. xi. 30` — a phrasing mismatch, not a negative result. Retry with our English wording.

### ✅ Printed 398 — the epigraph leaf, previously carrying NO sources at all, is now sourced
| our line | Brightman's identification |
|---|---|
| `ORATIONIS fundamentum et basis est fides. *Theophylact.*` | **Theophylact, *in S. Lucam* xviii** (ed. i. 433): `πάσης προσευχῆς βάθρον καὶ κρηπὶς ἡ πίστις` — ***βάθρον καὶ κρηπίς* = *fundamentum et basis*, exact.** |
| `Sursum corda.` | first in the **Hippolytean canons 3** (2nd–3rd cent.) and **Cyprian *de Orat. dom.* 31** |

Brightman also notes a lost wordplay in this neighbourhood — *fundit / fundatur*, closest parallel **Aug. *serm.* CXV 1**, *fides fundit orationem, fusa oratio fidei impetrat firmitatem*.

### ✅ Printed 386 (§41) — the authorities catena, sourced
`Cic. de senect. 11` (Cato's audit) · `Auson. Idyll.` · `Ps. lxxvii 6` · `Cp. Lucian Hermotimus 64` · `S. Aug. Serm. XX 2` · `Ecclus. xxiii 2` · `1 Cor. xi 31` · `S. Greg. Nyss. de orat. dom. 1`.
✅ **THE SENECA DIVERGENCE IS CLOSED (Wilson located it, 2026-08-04).** ***Seneca.*** is printed in the plate at **printed 385**, and the attribution is **correct**: sentence 1, `Deprehendas te oportet, antequam emendes`, is **Seneca, *Ep. Mor.* 28. 10**. **So the plate is right and Brightman's margin is simply short an authority** — his silence never indicated an error, and nothing here was ever ours to correct. ⚠ Seneca's own lead-in credits *«Initium est salutis notitia peccati»* to **EPICURUS**, which makes the §41 catena's chain **Epicurus → Seneca → Andrewes** — an introduction asset. ⚠⚠ **Sentence 2** (`Ignotum ulcus in deterius abit, et curatione destituitur`) is **not** in *Ep.* 28 and, on Wilson's search, **occurs ONLY IN ANDREWES** — so the one `*Seneca.*` tag covers two sentences of which **only the first is Seneca's**, the second amplifying his metaphor (the sore never found festers and goes uncured) and quite possibly being Andrewes' own. **Stated at the strength the evidence bears: unattested elsewhere, NOT "Andrewes' own"** — a florilegium or commonplace source is not excluded. **The tag is kept as printed** (§39 *Fulgentius* rule: an over-reaching attribution is flagged, never trimmed to fit); the note carries what the tag does not.

### ✅ Two of our Part III §1 divergences independently confirmed
- **`mundam`** — Brightman `P. 189. 6: H reads mundam; O, vincentem mundum` (§2.3).
- **FIVE Spirit-operations, no *Consolatione*** — Brightman's Part III text likewise gives *reproof, teaching, bearing with, help, witnessing with*. Our note recorded five against §23's six; **confirmed.**

### ✅ A class-B boundary corroborated
Class B marks two blank pages after **printed 190. 4**, at the close of *προαιρέσεις, ἐπιχειρήσεις, ἔξοδον καὶ εἴσοδον, κάθεδραν καὶ ἔγερσιν*. Brightman sets exactly that text as **a discrete titled unit** with the siglum **`L 134`** — *"I commend unto Thee, o Lord, impulses, occasions, purposes, endeavours, going out and coming in, downsitting and uprising."* **Independent corroboration of the class-B unit boundary at 190.4**, from the Laudian MS rather than the Wright apograph.

### Anchor table, extended
| Brightman p. | our printed p. | section |
|---|---|---|
| 106 | 386 | II §41 |
| ~131 | 357 | II §28 (the alms ladder) |
| ~147 | 409 ff. | III §2 |
| 189 | ~403 | III §1 |
| 192 | 370 | II §35 |
| ~196 | ~402 | III §1 (Creed, art. ii–iv) |
| 257 | 380 | II §39 |
| 289–290 (notes) | 398 | III §1 epigraph leaf |
| 337 | 371 | II §36 |

## 3b. ✅ THE RETRY PASS — 2026-08-09. **Part III §2's reference list is now fully adjudicated: 8 of 8.**

The 2026-08-04 pass closed on two no-hits and left six references "doubtful and unadjudicated." **All eight are now settled or improved**, from a single method change.

### ⚠ THE METHOD FINDING — search him by OUR ENGLISH, not by the Latin
Both 2026-08-04 no-hits were failures of the *query*, not of the witness. Brightman prints no Latin, so a Latin phrase can never match him; and his English is his own, so it will not match ours word for word either. **What does match is the SCRIPTURE WORDING**, because both of us are quoting the same English Bible — grep the AV/BCP phrase the line is built on (*"carest thou not that we perish"*, *"known in the dark"*, *"for mine own sake"*) and he surfaces immediately, margin and all. Once one line of a section is located, **his whole rendering of that section is contiguous** and every neighbouring reference comes free. Our printed 409–416 is his pp. 146–149, a dense line-by-line parallel. **This is much cheaper than the 2026-08-04 pass and should be the default shape for any further lookup.**

| our reference, as printed | status before | status now |
|---|---|---|
| `[Marc. iv. 28.]` (410) | no hit | ✅ **Mark iv. 38** confirmed, three times |
| `1 Cor. xi. 30.` (413) | no hit | ✅ **1 Cor. xi. 31** confirmed |
| `*Psal.* xl. 9.` (409) | doubtful; guessed Ps. xxxi. 10 | ⚠⚠ **REVERSED → Ps. lxxviii. 33** |
| `*Job.* xxx. 33.` (412) | doubtful | ✅ **Job xxxi. 33** confirmed |
| `liii. 13.` (415) | doubtful | ✅ **Ps. lxxxviii. 12** confirmed |
| `*Is.* xliii. 24.` (415) | doubtful | ✅ **Isaiah xliii. 25** confirmed |
| `*Num.* xiv. 7.` (416) | doubtful | ✅ **Num. xiv. 17–19** corroborated |
| `*Job.* xxv. 3.` (414) | doubtful | ⚠ **improved, NOT closed** — needs page image |

**Every one is kept as printed.** The transcripts are untouched; the notes now name verses instead of raising questions.

### ⚠⚠ The one real correction: we were wrong at printed 409
`*Psal.* xl. 9.` heads *Defecerunt in vanitate dies mei, et anni in anxietate cordis*, and our note proposed **Ps. xxxi. 10** as "closer." It is **Ps. lxxviii. 33** — Brightman cites it twice in unrelated parts of his book, and the Latin proves it without him: *Defecerunt in vanitate dies* is **verbatim** Vulgate Ps. lxxvii. 33, and *anni in anxietate* renders that verse's own second half. Ps. xxxi. 10 supplies neither half. ⚠ **A conjecture that reads plausibly is not a collation; this one survived two passes before a witness was actually asked.**

### ✅ THE ONE THAT RESISTED — CLOSED 2026-08-17: `*Job.* xxv. 3.` at printed 414
**Settled, and the page image was got.** Brightman's margin, read on the plate (`archive.org/details/bwb_KP-665-232`, printed p. 148 = leaf `n213`; the image endpoint is `archive.org/download/bwb_KP-665-232/page/nNNN.jpg`, and **printed page = n − 65** for this scan), reads **`Job xiv 4 vulg., iv 18`**. The OCR's `av 18` was `iv 18`; there is no third figure, and **he gives no reference at all for the stars clause**. ⚠ **His `vulg.` label disagrees with his own note** at his p. 143. 3 sq., which quotes Andrewes' Pentecost sermon: *infans unius diei super terram*, **`as the Seventy read it`** (Job xiv 4). The substance is settled without him and against the label — the Clementine Vulgate of Job xiv. 4–5 has no day-old child at all (verified: *Quis potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine? … Breves dies hominis sunt*), while the LXX does (*ἐὰν καὶ μία ἡμέρα ὁ βίος αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*), and Augustine gives it in that Latin at *Conf.* I. vii. 11. **So the cento is Job xiv. 4 (Sept.) + xxv. 5 (Vulg.) + iv. 18 (not Vulg., which reads *reperit pravitatem*; the plate's *insipientiam* is the Hebrew's word, as AV).** Brightman's *bare* `iv 18`, on his own version-flag convention, is itself the witness that the last clause follows the English Bible. Note applied at 414; nothing in any transcript touched.

### A by-product: a third witness to the BCP Psalter
Brightman numbers *"He considered that we are but flesh… a wind that passeth away"* as **Ps. lxxviii. 40** — in two margins and in his own printed psalm text — where the AV has **39**. That is the **Prayer Book Psalter's numbering**, one ahead through this psalm. It joins printed 433's `xlii. 10` and `lxv. 8` as evidence that the BCP was the book physically to hand, and it strengthens CONVENTIONS §9's Coverdale-first rule. It does **not** unsettle our own note at 411, which reads the plate's `lxviii. 39` on AV numbering with a dropped `x`.

⚠ **And a plate pattern worth recording:** Part III §2 misnumbers **Psalm lxxviii twice in seven pages** — at 409 (`xl. 9`) and 411 (`lxviii. 39`). Two corruptions of one psalm reads as a compositor's hand rather than an author's numbering, which is a small independent support for the standing "kept as printed, flagged, never mended" discipline.

## 4. Verdict on Wilson's question

**Yes — but question-driven, not linear.** Four hits from five probes, including one solved crux and one independent confirmation of a Part III structural finding, is a decisive pilot. A full linear collation is the wrong instrument and would cost many times more for less.

**✅ The flag-list pass was RUN on Opus, 2026-08-04, on Wilson's go — see §3a.** Three of the five watch items resolved or downgraded, four wrong references identified or confirmed, two Part III §1 divergences independently corroborated, one class-B boundary corroborated, and two previously unsourced pages (398, 386) sourced. **Nothing applied.**

**Still open after BOTH passes** (updated 2026-08-09): printed **210** and **239** (lost Latin/Greek words — digitization only, Brightman structurally cannot help) · printed **386**'s Hebrew (needs his page images) · printed **414**'s `Job. xxv. 3` cento (same blocker — his page image) · **`p. 207`** (an apparatus crux; Brightman cannot speak to it at all) · printed **370/371**'s missing *heading*, which he has but which is **his own and unusable**.

✅ **Closed since:** §41's Seneca (sentence 1 at *Ep. Mor.* 28. 10; sentence 2 unattested outside Andrewes) · **all eight of Part III §2's open references** (§3b).

⚠ **What the residue has in common: it is now almost entirely a SOURCE-IMAGE problem, not a collation problem.** Four of the five remaining items are blocked on the same thing — a non-Google digitization, plus Brightman's own page images for anything carried in italics. **Further text-only lookups have low expected yield; the next real gain comes from images.**

Related: `CLASS-A-ledger.md` · `CLASS-B-unit-boundaries.md` · `THE-LATIN-QUESTION.md` · `../EDITION-SHAPE.md` §4a.

# *Variæ Lectiones et Addenda Quædam* — raw transcript

Source: 1853 Parker ed., the apparatus following the primary text — **PDF 482–491**, images `raw/end/p-NNN.jpg`. The apparatus is **separately foliated in lower-case roman**: PDF 482 = **[i]** (unnumbered, the title page), 483 = **ii**, 484 = **iii**, and so on to PDF 491 = **x**. ⚠ **Do not address these pages by their PDF number in any ledger** — the apparatus's own `p. N. lin. N.` citations refer to **printed arabic pages of the primary text**, and confusing the two numbering systems would wreck the collation.

**This is a collation ledger, not primary text.** It is transcribed verbatim and it is NOT translated: the entries are the 1853 editor's Latin notes about a manuscript, addressed to a reader who has the book open. Class-A readings are resolved against our own files in `CLASS-A-ledger.md`; **nothing here is silently applied to any transcript.**

Transcription discipline: verbatim incl. accentuation; Greek per the standing rule (vision only, `[?]` where unreadable, **never inferred from context**); Hebrew given as printed, right-to-left, with a confidence note wherever the 200-dpi image cannot separate look-alike sorts (ד/ר, ב/כ); the editor's own italics preserved; `lin.` / `col.` / `sqq.` / `ult.` / `penult.` left unexpanded.

⚠ **THE DOT-MARKS.** The apograph indexes certain prayers with **marks made of dots** — one dot, two dots, three (∴), four (⸬), and apparently more. Where the count is legible it is given as that many `·` inside braces, e.g. `{···}`. **Where the arrangement cannot be resolved at 200 dpi it is given as `{·?}` and must not be guessed** — these marks are the manuscript's own index to the prayers and an invented arrangement would corrupt it. **NEW WATCH ITEM; see the notes at the foot of this file.**

---

        VARIÆ LECTIONES

        ADDENDA QUÆDAM
EX APOGRAPHO SAMUELIS WRIGHT,
        APUD COLL. PEMB. CANT.
                CONSERVATO.

QUATUOR hæc imprimis observata volumus :—

  i. Hoc apographum Græca tantum continet usque ad pag. 250

 ii. Nulli sunt tituli, præter Ὡσαννὰ ἐν ὑψίστοις, p. 208; Ὡσαννὰ

iii. Græcis literis, α΄, β΄, γ΄, (κ.τ.λ.) non Arabicis, notantur partes
distinctæ.

## Transcriber's notes

1. **Twenty-four notes in all**, covering printed pp. 16–246 — i.e. **entirely within Part I**, and entirely within the *usque ad pag. 250* range of the apograph. There is **no source-note anywhere in Parts II or III**, which is consistent with the apograph not extending there and is not evidence that those Parts are un-sourced.

2. **The liturgies named are three, and only three:**
   - **S. Chrysostom** — pp. 16, 18, 32, 54, 56, 118, 122, 138 (×2), 140, 238, 240
   - **S. James** — pp. 66, 116, 118, 124, 126, 140, 162
   - **S. Basil** — pp. 118, 240, 242, 244 (×2), 246

   ⚠ **The distribution is not random and should not be flattened into "the Eastern liturgies."** Chrysostom carries the morning and intercessory matter; **Basil is concentrated almost entirely in the eucharistic sequence at pp. 238–246** and appears nowhere before p. 118; James is spread thin across both. Three notes name **two** liturgies for one passage (pp. 118. 7; 140. 7; 240. 4) — Andrewes knew a phrase stood in more than one rite and said so.

3. ⚠ **The gap from p. 140 to p. 162, and again from p. 162 to p. 238, is in the manuscript, not in our transcription.** The two leaves are consecutive (PDF 492, 493) and nothing is missing between them. Do not read the gap as loss.

4. ⚠ **`p. 246. lin. 19. Ἥνωται`** carries the only note in which the editor supplies a **Greek rubric** rather than a page reference — `[Εὐχὴ ἐν τῷ συστεῖλαι τὰ ἅγια.]`, "the prayer at the veiling of the holy things." Bracketed, therefore the editor's, therefore **not evidence that Andrewes' MS named the rubric.**

5. **Editions cited by the 1853 editor** (all bracketed, all his): Goar, *Euchologion sive Rituale Græcorum*, Paris 1647; *Auctarium Bibliothecæ Patrum*, tom. ii, Paris 1624 (for St James). Both post-date Andrewes. **A pre-print check should confirm the Goar page numbers**, which are the only externally verifiable claims in this document — but that is a courtesy to the reader, not a correction to Andrewes.

title: The Latin Question
blurb: Whether the Latin of printed 1–250 is Andrewes' own or a 1675 editor's — surfaced, not settled; Wilson's call.
body:
# The Latin Question — the class-A test, run

**⚠ SURFACED, NOT ACTED ON.** Nothing in CONVENTIONS, no English, and no part of the Prototype B decision has been changed on the strength of this file. **It is Wilson's call and it is an introduction-level question, not a translation-level one.**

## The question

The apparatus preface (PDF 482, apparatus [i]) states:

> *Hoc apographum Græca tantum continet usque ad pag. 250 nostræ editionis, **sine versione Latina, quam Editor ipse confecisse videtur**.*
> — "This apograph contains only Greek as far as p. 250 of our edition, without the Latin version, **which the Editor himself seems to have made**."

If the Latin of printed 1–250 is an editor's Latin rather than something with independent standing, then for that stretch the Prototype B mirror sets Andrewes beside his editor, and "construal witness" means less than it has meant all along.

## The test the brief designed

Class A gives apograph-versus-printed-Greek divergences for exactly this stretch. For each one, **check which reading the facing Latin supports.**

- Latin **consistently follows the printed Greek** → it is downstream of the edited Greek, and the question is settled: editor's Latin.
- Latin **ever supports the apograph against the printed Greek** → it has a source independent of the printed Greek, and the preface's *videtur* is too modest.

## The result: **the second branch fires.**

Ten divergences were resolved against our own transcripts. **Five** support the printed Greek, **two** support the apograph, **three** cannot decide.

| # | class A | printed Greek | apograph reads | facing Latin | supports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | p. 6. 20 | `τοῦ ἁγίου φροντιστηρίου τούτου` | `τῆς ἁγίας μονῆς ταύτης` | *hujus sacri **Collegii*** (7) | **printed** |
| 2 | p. 12. 26 | `Τέμενος Βασιλικόν` | *dele* `Βασιλικόν` | *Sacellum **Regium*** (13) | **printed** |
| 3 | p. 26. 26 | `Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἀληθείας` | `ὁ Θεὸς` not in MS | *Domine, **Deus** veritatis* (27) | **printed** |
| 4 | **p. 34. 27** | `Τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σου` | `τὸ πλάσμα` | ***Figmenta** manuum tuarum* (35) | **APOGRAPH** |
| 5 | p. 50. 18 | `ἀπὸ τῆς προσδοκίας` | `ἐλπίδος` | *ab hac mea **exspectatione*** (51) | **printed** |
| 6 | p. 100. 7 | `Βουλευτὰς` | `συμβουλευτάς` | ***Consiliarios*** (101) | apograph (weak) |
| 7 | p. 162. 16 | `ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν` | `ὑπερβάλλουσα` | *quæ **exsuperat** omnem sensum* (163) | inconclusive |
| 8 | p. 170. 16 | `τὰς ἀνομίας μου` | `ἁμαρτίας` | ***iniquitates** meas* (171) | **printed** |
| 9 | **p. 174. 13** | `ἀπόλυσαι` | `ἀπόλουσαι` | ***Ablue*** (175) | **APOGRAPH** |
| 10 | p. 224. 8 | `ἡ θυσία ἑσπερινή` | `δειλινή` | *Sacrificium **vespertinum*** (225) | inconclusive |

**Why 7 and 10 cannot decide:** both Latin words are **Vulgate lemmata** for the verses being quoted — *exsuperat* is the Vulgate's own word at Phil. iv. 7, and *sacrificium vespertinum* is the Vulgate's at Ps. cxl. 2. A translator would write them whichever Greek stood in front of him. (10 is further spoiled because the Latin renders the heading `ΟΜΟΛΟΓΗΣΙΣ ΔΕΙΛΙΝΗ` as *CONFESSIO VESPERTINA* on the same spread — so *vespertinus* covers both Greek words in this translator's usage.)

## ⚠ Case 4 is the one that matters, and it is very hard to explain away

`Τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σου μὴ παρίδῃς` is **Ps. cxxxviii. 8**, and the Vulgate of that verse reads ***opera** manuum tuarum ne despicias*.

So a Latin made from the printed Greek would read *opera*. A Latin made by a translator who did not know the Greek and simply reached for his Vulgate would **also** read *opera*. A translator silently repairing a corruption by sense would reach for *opera* too, because that is the phrase every reader knows.

**The 1853 Latin reads *Figmenta*.**

*Figmentum* is the standard Latin for **πλάσμα** — the thing moulded — and it is exactly what the apograph reads. The Latin has departed from the printed Greek **and** from the Vulgate **and** from the reader's expectation, and landed on the manuscript. There is no route to *Figmenta* that does not pass through a Greek text reading πλάσμα.

**Case 9 is the corroboration.** `ἀπόλυσαι` ("release") stands in a column of cleansing verbs — *Tege · Ablue · Dele · Purga* answering `κάλυψον · ἀπόλυσαι · ἐξάλειψον · καθάρισον`, all under the head `Τὸ ῥυπαρὸν / Macula`, the stain. **`Ablue` is "wash away" and cannot come from ἀπόλυσαι**; it renders the apograph's `ἀπόλουσαι`, which differs by a single letter and is manifestly the true reading. This one *could* be a competent translator repairing an obvious corruption by sense — but it repairs it to precisely the manuscript's letter.

## What this does and does not establish

**Does:** the 1853 Latin of printed 1–250 is **not purely downstream of the printed Greek**. At least once it witnesses a Greek reading found in the manuscript, absent from the printed text, and absent from the Vulgate. The preface's *videtur* is too modest, exactly as the brief anticipated it might be.

**Does not:** it does not show the Latin is Andrewes'. Five of ten cases follow the printed Greek, which is what one expects if the Latin and the printed Greek largely share a source. The likeliest reading of the whole pattern is that **the Latin was made from a Greek text closer to the apograph than the printed text is** — and that where the two now differ, the printed edition, not the Latin, is the one that has moved.

**Still open, and not to be flattened:**
- **Which Editor?** The brief's argument that *Editor* most naturally means the **1675** Sheldonian editor (contrasted with *nostra editio* = 1853) still stands and is untouched by this test.
- ⚠ **The class A / class C collisions** (see `CLASS-A-ledger.md` §4) are a real complication and are **not resolved here.** At several lines — pp. 34. 27, 50. 18, 104. 3, 116. 9, 162. 16, 170. 16, 190. 13, 224. 8 — a class-A reading and a Drake marginal address the same words, and the direction of class C's `]` cannot be settled from the printed apparatus alone. **Do not build an argument on the collisions until the manuscript itself has been seen.**

## What changes

**Almost nothing, and that was true before the test.** CONVENTIONS §6 already makes the Greek primary and the Latin *the first witness to construal* — a role this result strengthens rather than weakens. Prototype B reproduces the 1675 book, which is what it always claimed to do. The project's framing — "Greek original, historic Latin parallel, fresh English translation" — is accurate under any answer.

**What genuinely changes is the introduction**, and there it is now an asset: the edition can say, with a worked example, that its Latin column is an independent witness and not a shadow of its Greek. That is a stronger claim than the project has ever been able to make, and it is now evidenced.

✅ **RE-CHECKED AND CONFIRMED 2026-08-10 — the argument's one load-bearing word is secure.** Case 4 (`Figmenta` / `τὸ πλάσμα`, printed 34/35) was on the pre-print list because the whole case rests on reading a single word correctly. The apparatus entry was re-read on the University of Toronto scan (leaf 0480, apparatus ii): **`p. 34. lin. 27. pro τὰ ἔργα lege τὸ πλάσμα et dele punctum post παριδῇς, et in lin. 28. lege ὁμοίωμα puncto adjecto.`** — unambiguous at native resolution, and our transcript matches it exactly. **The reading may now be printed in an introduction. Off the pre-print list.**
